text.p: A Saudi collector who already owns the largest diamond ever sold at auction on Wednesday paid 1.38 million swiss francs ($996,030) for part of the French crown jewels, including a sapphire and diamond tiara, Sotheby's said.
Ahmed Fitaihi attended the Geneva sale, where he also bought the evening's top lot, a pear-shaped blue diamond ring weighing 5.07 carats for 3.08 million swiss francs ($2.2 million).
Fitaihi, who lives in Jeddah, also paid nearly 500,000 swiss francs ($359,190) for a stunning diamond tiara made by the jeweller Cartier in 1920, one of the evening's main lots.
"I got everything I wanted," Fitaihi told Reuters. "I'll keep it for my private collection."

The mid-19th century French royal parure, comprising the tiara, matching earrings, brooches, corsage ornament and centre plaque of a bracelet, belonged to Queen Marie-Amelie of France (1782-1866), wife of King Louis-Philippe d'Orleans. It was sold by the Comte de Paris, head of the royal house of Orleans.

"It is interesting that the parure has passed into private hands after 130 years. It may be the last piece of French royal jewellery to appear on the market," David Bennett, head of Sotheby's jewellery department, told reporters.
